title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #799: List Chromatic Number of Random Graphs. Status: SOLVED (Alon 1992, Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov 1999)

title: Colorlistassignment
content: A function assigning to each vertex a finite set of available colors.

title: Isvalidlistcoloring
content: A coloring where each vertex receives a color from its list, and adjacent vertices receive distinct colors. (f : V → C) : Prop := (∀ v, f v ∈ L v) ∧ (∀ v w, G.Adj v w → f v ≠ f w)

title: Islistcolorable
content: A graph G is k-list colorable if for any assignment of lists of size k to each vertex, a valid list coloring exists. ∀ (C : Type) [DecidableEq C] (L : ColorListAssignment V C), (∀ v, (L v).card ≥ k) → ∃ f : V → C, IsValidListColoring G L f

title: Listchromaticnumber
content: χ_L(G) is the minimum k such that G is k-list colorable. sInf {k : ℕ | IsListColorable G k}

title: List Chromatic Ge Chromatic
content: The list chromatic number is at least the ordinary chromatic number. This is because we can give every vertex the same list of χ(G) colors. listChromaticNumber G ≥ G.chromaticNumber

title: List Chromatic Gap Unbounded
content: There exist bipartite graphs (χ = 2) with arbitrarily large χ_L. The complete bipartite graph K_{n,n} satisfies χ_L(K_{n,n}) ≥ ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1. ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = 2 ∧ listChromaticNumber G ≥ k

title: Listchromaticrandom
content: The list chromatic number of a graph on n vertices drawn from G(n, 1/2). We axiomatize the almost-sure behavior rather than the probability model.

title: Chromatic Number Random Graph
content: For G ∈ G(n, 1/2), χ(G) ≍ n / (2 log₂ n) almost surely. ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, c₁ > 0 ∧ c₂ > 0 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → c₁ * (n : ℝ) / Real.log n ≤ (listChromaticRandom n : ℝ)

title: Alon 1992
content: For the random graph G on n vertices with edge probability 1/2: χ_L(G) ≪ (log log n / log n) · n almost surely.  This was the first proof that χ_L(G) = o(n) for random graphs, using the probabilistic method and the Lovász Local Lemma. ∃ C : ℝ, C > 0 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → (listChromaticRandom n : ℝ) ≤ C

title: List Chromatic Sublinear
content: Alon's theorem implies that χ_L(G) grows slower than linearly in n. ∀ ε : ℝ, ε > 0 → ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ N₀ → (listChromaticRandom n : ℝ) ≤ ε * n

title: Alon Krivelevich Sudakov 1999
content: Alon, Krivelevich, and Sudakov (1999) proved that for G ∈ G(n, 1/2): χ_L(G) ≍ n / log n almost surely.  More precisely: - Upper bound: χ_L(G) ≤ C₁ · n / log n (semi-random / Rödl nibble method) - Lower bound: χ_L(G) ≥ C₂ · n / log n (adversarial list construction) ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, C₁ > 0 ∧ C₂ > 0 ∧ ∀ n

title: List Vs Ordinary Ratio
content: For G ∈ G(n, 1/2): - χ(G) ≈ n / (2 log₂ n) - χ_L(G) ≍ n / log n  So χ_L(G) / χ(G) → 2 / ln 2 ≈ 2.885 as n → ∞. The list chromatic number exceeds the ordinary one by a constant factor. ∀ ε : ℝ, ε > 0 → ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ N₀ → |(listChromaticRandom n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) / Real.log n) - 1| ≤ ε

title: Erdos 799
content: Question: Is χ_L(G) = o(n) for almost all graphs on n vertices?  Answer: YES  For the random graph G(n, 1/2): 1. Alon (1992): χ_L(G) ≪ (log log n / log n) · n 2. AKS (1999): χ_L(G) ≍ n / log n  Both bounds show χ_L(G) = o(n) almost surely. ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, C₁ > 0 ∧ C₂ > 0 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → C₂ * (n : ℝ)
